name: Saint Philip Neri
history: A Florentine who came to Rome as a young man and became its apostle, drawing people of every kind to God by friendship, prayer and laughter. He founded the Congregation of the Oratory, whose informal gatherings of prayer, Scripture and music gave the oratorio its name. Cheerful and humble, he is one of the best loved saints of Rome.
life: Philip was born in Florence and taught by the Dominicans at San Marco. At eighteen he was sent to learn business from a relative, but soon left for Rome, where he lived very simply, tutored two boys, and spent nights praying in the catacombs. At Pentecost 1544, in the catacomb of San Sebastiano, he felt a ball of fire enter his heart, and his heart was said to beat visibly ever after. For years he worked as a layman, talking to people in the streets and shops and founding a confraternity to care for pilgrims. Ordained in 1551, he heard confessions for hours each day. In a room above his church he gathered men to pray, read, discuss and sing, and from this came the Oratory, approved in 1575. He used jokes to keep himself and others humble. John Henry Newman brought the Oratory to England.
prayerTo: Saint Philip, you won souls by kindness and joy, and kept them humble with a smile. Pray for the city of Rome, for priests and confessors, and for the Oratories. Give me a cheerful heart, a love for prayer and the sacraments, and the grace not to take myself too seriously. Amen.
penance: Make a good confession if you can, as Philip urged his friends to do often. Do something today to cheer someone who is low, and laugh at yourself once.
meditation: He would wear his clothes inside out or shave half his beard so that no one would think him a saint. What would it cost you to look foolish for God?
prayer: O God, Who raised blessed Philip, Your Confessor, to the glory of Your Saints, graciously grant that we who rejoice in his feast may profit by the example of his virtues. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
